chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The sense of honor (ghayrah) is not except for the men, and as for the women, then that from them is envy. And the sense of honor is for the men, and for that reason Allah prohibited it upon the women, except for her husband, and He permitted for the men four (wives), and indeed Allah is more Benevolent than that He would test them with the sense of honor and permit for the men along with her three (more).

key_terms.الْغَيْرَةُ: Sense of honor or jealousy, specifically regarding a spouse's fidelity
key_terms.ثَلَاثاً: Three (referring to additional wives beyond the first)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between ghayrah and hasad in Shia jurisprudence regarding men and women?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between 'ghayrah' (protective jealousy/honor) as a male trait and 'hasad' (envy) as the female equivalent, linking this psychological distinction to the legal allowance of polygyny for men. This interpretation reflects the Shia scholarly view that the permissibility of four wives for men is a concession of ease rather than a burden, as women are not subjected to the same 'test' of managing multiple spouses. The narration underscores divine benevolence by tailoring marital laws to the inherent dispositions of each gender.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The sense of ‘الْغَيْرَةُ’ (honour of lineage) is not for anyone except for the men, and as for the women, so that (sense of honour) from them is envy, and the sense of honour is for the men, and it is due to that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Prohibited it upon the women, except that He<sup>azwj</sup> Got her to be married and Permitted four (wives) for the men, and that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Benevolent than that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Try them with the sense of honour and He<sup>azwj</sup> has Permitted three (more wives) for the men along with her’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Pride is with men only and with women it is jealousy. Vanity is with men and for this reason Allah has prohibited women except to have one husband and for men He has made up to four (wives) lawful. Allah is most gracious. He does not place vanity and pride in them (women) then make three more with her lawful for him/”
